title: One gateway checks the inventory, pins the model and keeps each draft for audit
subtitle: Example: a made-up Swiss bank drafts a meeting note after a client call. The OpenAI names and terms are real.
aria: An adviser's notes service sends a prompt with three headers to an AI gateway, the only service with the OpenAI keys. The gateway refuses any call with no approved inventory row, calls the pinned snapshot in OpenAI's Europe region, stores the prompt and the draft in a content store and inserts a call row. The adviser's edit is inserted later as a separate event row. The row's risk class adds controls, and fourteen months later audit answers five questions from these records.

build.title: The adviser and the notes service
build.text: The adviser `rm.jmuster` presses "draft note". The notes service `advisory-notes` stops an empty transcript, then sends the prompt with 3 headers: use case, prompt version and user.

build.title: One gateway checks the inventory
build.text: The AI gateway alone holds the OpenAI keys. It looks up the inventory row for this use case and caller. With no row it refuses and sends nothing. The row pins the model and the region.

build.title: A pinned snapshot at OpenAI
build.text: The gateway calls `gpt-4o-2024-08-06`, a fixed, dated build, in OpenAI's Europe region. The alias `gpt-4o` moves to newer builds, so the row never names one. If OpenAI reports another model, the gateway alerts.

build.title: Records that are never updated
build.text: Before it returns, the gateway stores the prompt and the draft in an encrypted content store and inserts a call row. The adviser's edit is a new event row, so the draft stays as written.

build.title: The risk class adds controls
build.text: The bank's example rule puts each use case in a class. Medium, the meeting note, adds the Europe region, no copy at OpenAI and an eval each release. High adds zero data retention and a named approver.

build.title: Audit asks five questions
build.text: 14 months later, audit asks which model, what it wrote, where the data went, whether it was tested and signed, and whether it still works. Each answer is in a record.

route.title: The notes service checks the transcript and names its use case
route.text: The notes service refuses an empty or cut-off transcript. Then it sends the prompt with its own service credential. Three headers name the use case, the prompt version v7 and the user `rm.jmuster`.

route.title: The gateway finds the inventory row or refuses the call
route.text: If no row has this use case with this credential, the call is refused and nothing reaches OpenAI. The row gives the risk class Medium, the model and the Europe region, so the caller cannot choose them.

route.title: The gateway calls a pinned snapshot and checks what answered
route.text: It calls the snapshot `gpt-4o-2024-08-06`, never the alias `gpt-4o`, and records the version OpenAI reports. A mismatch alerts the row's owner. On a High row it also refuses the call.

route.title: The gateway stores the draft itself
route.text: A rerun may give a different draft. So the prompt and the draft go into the encrypted content store, and a call row that is never updated points at them. The draft goes back with `call_id` c-81f2.

route.title: The adviser's edit becomes a new row
route.text: The notes service keeps the final note `note/44120` in its own store and inserts an event row keyed by c-81f2. The draft in the content store stays as the model wrote it.

route.title: Fourteen months later, audit reads the answers from rows
route.text: Audit follows the note to c-81f2. The call row names the snapshot, the prompt version and the region. The content store holds the draft before the edit, and the event row shows who changed it.
